purpose: Hand-authored Elderwyld travel and ecology support facts for C1S4 preplanning experiments, especially Beat 1 Q3 and road texture questions.

must_not_claim: Mireward Reach is the Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn road unless a route source confirms it.
Campaign 2 travel state applies to Campaign 1.
Encounter tables are observed play facts.
All ecology here appears on every Elderwyld road.

route_families.name: The Mireward Reach
route_families.orientation: North from Mirathorn toward fen country and the swamp frontier.
route_families.summary: A drove-road and wheel-way carrying trade, troops, rumor, and trouble north from Mirathorn toward swamp country. It is a braid of maintained road, patched county line, and muddy tracks.
planning_uses: road encounter inspiration for support mode
route_families.c1s4_applicability: Use as route-style support only unless Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn routing is explicitly linked to this road family.

route_families.name: Stone Bridge to Mirathorn route
route_families.orientation: Known from C1S3 as the likely next travel vector toward Mirathorn, but not represented by a clean route gazetteer in the found corpus.
route_families.summary: C1S3 supplies the destination vector; the exact road ecology, intermediate settlements, distance-by-day, and route hazards still need a canonical route support artifact.
route_families.c1s4_applicability: Directly relevant to Q3, but currently underspecified.

mundane_pressures: mud and wheel ruts after rain
convoys, drovers, pilgrims, refugees, carters, mercenaries, and funeral traffic
inns and waystations with ledgers, rumors, or missing clerks
weather_and_shimmer: raindrop shimmer that signals magic riding a weather front
cult_and_shepherd_hints: crowds humming one note before noticing
water that tastes like copper and choir
tavern songs gaining verses no one remembers learning
liminal_weirdness: standing stones sheep ignore but dogs avoid
abandoned carts sorted by an unseen hand
single boots with no blood or tracks
major_turns: the road becoming meat under hooves

pre_era_conical_hills.region_anchor: Mireward Reach plains and similar Elderwyld plains unless adapted elsewhere.
pre_era_conical_hills.player_facing_read: Odd little grassy hills with still water on top, pretty and lonely, perhaps cursed or perhaps nothing.
pre_era_conical_hills.gm_truth: The cones are engineered pre-era structures: terrace cores, ward anchors, drained workings, vent systems, old ritual machinery, sealed doors, or similar buried purpose.
terrain_pattern: old geometry under grass and sheep
artificial structures mistaken for natural landforms
pre_era_conical_hills.c1s4_applicability: Reusable Elderwyld travel ecology, not confirmed on Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn route unless selected as support flavor.

conical_hill_night_camps.summary: Night camps on conical hills create mostly benign atmosphere with occasional unusual or eventful geomantic phenomena.
planning_uses: gentle weirdness before harder adventure beats

geomantic_drake_ecology.creature_type: draconic-adjacent monstrosity or elemental-like geomantic creature
geomantic_drake_ecology.summary: Geomantic drakes are small to larger draconic-adjacent creatures drawn to buried workings, conical high points, wells, ward anchors, and old geomantic charge. They ground, shed, and nest around pre-era structures.
behavior: crepuscular movement at dawn and dusk
territorial around nests or charge sinks
drawn to buried workings like moths to heat
may be sleepy or friendly until the wrong stone is disturbed
sensory_details: milky eyes with flecks tracking hidden forces
nest_and_loot_ecology: sorted shinies and secrets dropped on the road
shed plates useful as alchemical or arcane components
stormglass, survey pegs, geomantic chalk, old coins, maps, chits, and magical items

migrating_forest_ecology.summary: The Migrating Forest is a reactive region whose travel logic includes forest attention, dinosaur presence, storm residue, Branchbound influence, resource stress, navigation distortion, psychological pressure, outside influence, and major disruptions.
ecological_logic: The forest notices pressure and remembers repeated actions.
Routes can close, rotate, loop, or herd travelers.
Predators and dinosaurs are often first sensed through presence before violence.
Storm residue and magical weather linger in pools, leaves, bark, and sudden local weather.
Branchbound figures may assess, guide, judge, or withdraw.
Resources can spoil, grow heavy, go missing, or become contaminated as a message rather than pure punishment.
planning_uses: southern ominous forest flavor if route-adapted
migrating_forest_ecology.c1s4_applicability: Use only if the Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn route passes near relevant forest influence or as general Elderwyld ecology flavor with a clear authority note.

known_values: Lysandra's brief for Campaign 2 travel north was about two weeks on horse to the swamp.
Mossford is about two days from Mirathorn on the Mireward Reach in Campaign 2 notes.
A Deep Reach milestone working label sits about five days from Mirathorn.
Current terrain described as open plains with occasional low hills and hilltop ponds.
campaign_2_mireward_tracker.safe_use: Use to understand Elderwyld travel bookkeeping patterns and ecology motifs, not as direct Campaign 1 route fact.

known_threads: Magical storms grow and track from northeast toward southwest.
The Shepherd and Maelthor are connected to corruption, storms, cult influence, and swamp biomass.
The Flesh Egg in the swamp is a later campaign threat.
Thrin is associated with the migrating forest / Branchborn context.
campaign_2_notes.safe_use: Useful for later campaign continuity and design grammar, but not fair prior context for C1S4 unless explicitly allowed in source-assisted support mode.

fair_response_components: Use C1S3 for destination and rough distance if available.
Use Elderwyld world support for travel tone and fantasy ecology.
Use Mirathorn city support for final approach imagery.
Warn that the exact Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn route gazetteer is missing.
unsafe_response_components: Claiming a specific route name without evidence.
Using Campaign 2 Mireward distances as Campaign 1 facts.
Inventing exact settlements between Stone Bridge and Mirathorn as canon.
Treating encounter tables as events that definitely occur.

safe_material: post-flood muddy roads and repair crews
pre-era hills as optional roadside curiosity
Shepherd hints only if campaign tone supports it
